text:
alexa: Heads-up — ACME reported missing audit events around an RBAC change yesterday. they see the UI showing a role assignment but no matching audit row in the dump. pinging @security-oncall and @mike for quick triage.

security-oncall: on it. which org/environment?

alexa: acme-corp-prod, org_id=8429. customer timestamps 2024-05-10T14:03:21Z -> 2024-05-10T14:05:03Z, they provided UI screenshot and local app log.

mike: i'll pull audit-archive for that range now. also will check KMS rotation windows and any ingest errors.

sre-bot: deploy:service/audit-ingest version=v2.1.0 completed by mike at 2024-05-09T02:12:14Z :white_check_mark:

jordan: quick note — we rolled a schema tweak in v2 that renamed actor_id -> actor_principal and added actor_type. older services might still emit actor_id; ingestion has a temporary compatibility layer but it was disabled in canary.

emma: +1 — we disabled the compatibility adapter during the v2 rollout window because it was masking a validation bug. that rollout finished 02:12Z but a small % of instances were still on v1 for ~2h during autoscale.

alexa: customer says UI shows role assigned at 2024-05-10T14:04:00Z in their logs, but our audit query returned nothing. can you confirm if events were dropped or just indexed differently?

mike: searching audit-archive for org=8429, event_type=role_assignment, 2024-05-10T14:00:00Z..2024-05-10T14:10:00Z

mike: initial find: a few role_assignment events exist but they have actor_id as integer and org as string "8429" vs numeric filter used by the support query. also some events were routed to the legacy index prefix (audit-legacy-2024).

jordan: here's an example of two event payloads I grabbed from raw S3: one from pre-rollout, one post-rollout. note the field names and org typing.

jordan: ```
# pre-rollout (v1)
{
  "event_type": "role_assignment",
  "timestamp": "2024-05-10T14:04:01Z",
  "actor_id": 51234,
  "resource": "project:acme:env/prod",
  "org": "8429",
  "correlation_id": "c-7b3f"
}

# post-rollout (v2)
{
  "event_type": "role_assignment",
  "timestamp": "2024-05-10T14:04:02Z",
  "actor_principal": "user:alice@acme.com",
  "actor_type": "user",
  "resource": "project:acme:env/prod",
  "org": 8429,
  "correlation_id": "c-7b3f"
}
```

emma: that matches the timing I expected. the compatibility adapter would have normalized actor_id -> actor_principal and coerced org types; since it was disabled during canary tail, some events landed without normalization and our support tooling filters missed them.

mike: confirming — events were not dropped, they were indexed under legacy prefix and used older field names/types so the support query (which filters org as int and index=audit-main-*) returned zero rows.

alexa: okay — customer-facing implication: timeline we sent to ACME omitted the role assignment. need to reconstruct and provide corrected timeline and apology. also need to ensure future queries are robust.

security-oncall: proposed immediate actions:
1) backfill and reindex the missing events for org=8429 from audit-legacy-2024 into audit-main with normalization.
2) re-enable a lightweight normalization shim at ingestion to accept both actor_id and actor_principal and coerce org to string+int canonical form.
3) add a support query fallback to search both index prefixes and both org types for 30d.
4) add automated test in release gate to validate new schema + legacy compatibility.

mike: I can implement the shim + tests. plan: small lambda that runs at ingest to detect actor_id and convert to actor_principal, and to emit a normalized_org string and org_int when convertible. will PR today EOD.

jordan: I'll open a docs PR to note the dual-format behavior and update the audit schema page and the API compatibility notes. also add a note for support query snippets.

alexa: i'll own the backfill for ACME. i'll run a targeted reindex for 2024-05-10T14:00..14:10 and produce a corrected timeline, then share with support to issue to the customer.

security-oncall: filing incident SEC-427 and linking this thread: https://tracker.internal/SEC-427 — labeling as customer-impact P2. action owners: alexa (backfill), mike (ingest shim + tests), jordan (docs).

emma: small follow-up — we should also add a regression eval that injects synthetic v1 events into the v2 ingestion path and asserts normalization. i'll pair with mike on the test harness.

sre-bot: ticket SEC-427 created by security-oncall at 2024-05-10T16:12:45Z :page_facing_up:

alexa: timeline ETA: backfill run + customer note draft within 3h.

mike: shim PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-ingest/pull/120 — basic conversion + tests, queued for review.

jordan: docs PR: github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/334 — added compatibility notes and support query examples.

security-oncall: thanks all. prioritize delivery today and @support-team will hold customer comms until alexa confirms corrected timeline. :thumbsup:

alexa: ack.

mike: ack.

emma: ack.
